title: Vexana of the Aspirants
mood: Torn from her happiest memory, Vexana is shown a future, and makes a choice she will tell no one.

hero.alt: A huge head armored in dark violet, crowned with spikes and horns, looks out through a tear in a blue sky, its eyes glowing violet.
hero.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 36

segs.t: Guinevere came apart with the sky. Her raised fist went first, then her grin. Then the grass beside Vexana was empty. Her own hand still hung in the air, half raised from the pat.
The blue split wider, like paper. The silver blades pushed through, and behind them came a hand as big as the tree. An arm followed, and a head rose up through the tear.

It was armored in dark violet and crowned with tall spikes and horns. Two violet eyes glowed in it. A thin streak of light ran sideways from one of them. Only the head, the shoulders and that one arm fit through the tear. The rest of it stayed in the dark behind.
Its shadow fell across the lawn. The green drained out of the leaves and the grass. Everything under it went violet, then black.
Vexana had fallen back on her hands in the grass. She did not remember falling.

media.alt: Vexana has fallen back on her hands in the grass, staring up in terror as a dark shadow drains the green around her.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 37

segs.t: The Will of the Planet,
she thought. It came out of the Enders’ dark, wearing their color, bigger than any of them.
Chang’e had called it the mind behind the Enders. Nobody had ever seen it. In class it had been a word on a screen. Now it was looking at her.
She dragged her staff off her back and fired. The shot went into the dark of its face and was gone. Not one plate moved.
The staff shook in her hands. Her breath came short and high. She could not look away from it.
“Look.”
The Will had no mouth to say it with. The word came out of the dark itself.
The lawn was gone.
A city burned under a black sky. In the middle of it stood the Academy’s tower, and blasts went off around the ring at its top, one after another.
High above the tower the sky had torn open. Through the smoke and the tear, something vast and winged was coming down.
Vexana knew it only from the same lesson. Chang’e had called it the Will’s body, as far as her readings could tell. It could only be the Mother Matrix.
She was on her knees in rubble. Her uniform was torn at the shoulder. Bruises ran down her arms, and her white gloves were gray with dust.
A few steps away, Guinevere lay face down among the broken stones. The others lay near her. None of them moved.
Guinevere’s arm was flung out toward her. Her black-gloved hand lay open in the dust, the glove torn across the back. One red bow hung loose and crooked in her hair.

media.alt: Blasts burst around the ring at the top of the Academy's tower under a smoky sky; then Guinevere lies face down among broken stones, the others fallen beyond her.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana motion comic

segs.t: I straighten it every morning,
thought Vexana.
“Get up,” she whispered. “Guinevere. Get up.”
Her legs would not carry her those few steps. Behind her something exploded, and grit rained into her hair.
She held the Emblem cupped in both hands in her lap. Her tears fell on it, one, then another. It did not light.
It lit only when Guinevere’s did. Nothing answered it now.

media.alt: Bruised hands in dusty white gloves cup a small star badge in her lap, a tear falling onto it.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 5

segs.t: The words came out of the smoke above her. Each one hung there, black, its edges fraying.
“Vexana of The Aspirants, you have reached the end of your future.”
“You shall witness life’s destruction, as all returns to chaos.”
“This is no judgment, merely the universe’s predetermined execution.”
The star cracked in her cupped hands.
The crack ran straight down its middle. It followed the seam Guinevere had soldered a hair crooked, the one Vexana’s fingertip had found on the rooftop.
Vexana pressed the two halves together. They would not hold.
No,
she thought.
She made this. She made it for me.
The halves crumbled into sparks in her palms. The sparks went out.
Her hands were empty. She kept them cupped anyway, around nothing, and the city went on burning without a sound.
Then there was only black.
She was on her knees in the void. Her wings had gone out. She knelt on nothing at all.
Her collar was warm. She touched it with shaking fingers. The Emblem was there. It was whole, and lit, faint and gold.
The Will was still there, huge in the dark. Its two violet eyes hung over her. It said nothing more.
She looked past it, into the dark behind it. The void. The place the Enders came from, where nobody could follow. She was inside it. And the mind behind them all was right in front of her.
Vexana’s lips moved before she knew she would speak.
“Is this...”
Her voice shook. She swallowed.
“...the only way to protect Guinevere?”

media.alt: Close on one of Vexana's violet eyes, wide open in the dark.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 38
Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 38

segs.t: It did not answer. It drew back into the dark the way a tide goes out, and the dark closed where it had been. She heard her answer in the silence anyway.
In the fall she had thought her debt was paid. Guinevere’s glove had been whole at the door, and that had been enough. Now she had seen it torn open in the dust. Saving her once had changed nothing.
It sends every Ender,
she thought.
It knows where they will strike. And it has no need to lie to me. I am alone in its dark. It could close that hand on me.
In the vision she had worn her uniform. She had been there, a few steps from Guinevere, still an Aspirant. They had lost anyway. Even the star had gone dark.
Hurt the Enders badly and they went quiet for a while. Every battle they had won this year had ended that way.
Every win only buys a lull,
she thought.
And a lull always ends.
Chang’e had given them one way to win: destroy the Enders’ Control Core, hidden in its dark void. And Vexana had said it herself, under the tree.
But we can’t get near the void.
The Will had broken in at that one memory, just as Guinevere swore to destroy the Core.
So the Core is real,
thought Vexana.
And it matters to it.
Under all of it lay the oldest thing. Her father had died for her. One wish had sat under everything she did since that day at the wall.
If only it had been me instead.
This time it could be.
And she could tell no one.
Partners tell each other first.
She had promised it, flat on the training-hall floor.
Not this.
Guinevere would never let her go alone. Guinevere would find a way, as she had said under the tree. She would find a way straight into this dark, after her.
Vexana gripped her staff and got one foot under her.
It kept me alive for something,
she thought.
Then let it use me.
She would take the Will’s orders, walk among its Enders as one of them, and keep close to its body.
The Mother Matrix would come down. She had just watched it come.
At the Academy everyone learned the first rule of Enders. They open their weak spot only when they strike. The chest plates split, and the core shows.
When the Matrix opened its chest to fire, she meant to be within reach. All of her aspirant power would go into that open core at once.
It would end her too. She looked at that once, and went on.
If the Control Core lay anywhere in this dark, she would take it first.
From the Academy’s side she could not stop it. From the Enders’ side, she might.
Vexana looked into the dark where the Will had gone.
“This destiny is mine to bear.”
Then she stood up in the dark.
